Meet Anna.

Anna Zhu is a pianist, MTNA-certified piano educator, and the founder of Fly to the Moon Piano & Music Studio. She holds a master’s degree in Communication and Public Relations from Johns Hopkins University and has completed additional coursework in Child Psychology and Introduction to Psychology through Coursera, as well as online coursework focused on children with autism through the University of British Columbia.

Read Anna's full approach

Her teaching experience includes working with children and adults of different ages, learning styles, and musical goals, including children on the autism spectrum and older adults living with dementia. These experiences have shaped her belief that there is no single “right” way to learn music. Patience, communication, trust, and an understanding of each student are at the heart of her teaching.

Anna continues her own advanced piano studies with Victoria Bogdashevskaya, former principal pianist of the Seattle Symphony, bringing an active connection to professional musicianship into her teaching.

At Fly to the Moon, Anna hopes to create more than piano lessons. She wants each student to feel heard, supported, challenged, and inspired—to develop strong musical foundations while discovering a personal and lasting connection with music.

Studio

Fly to the Moon Piano & Music Studio is a private teaching studio located in the 98059 area of Newcastle/Bellevue, Washington, serving students from Renton and surrounding communities.

Centered around a grand piano, the studio is designed to provide a calm, welcoming, and focused environment where students can step away from everyday distractions and connect deeply with music.

Whether a student is playing their very first note or preparing for an advanced performance, the studio is a place where curiosity is encouraged, mistakes are part of learning, and every musical milestone deserves to be celebrated.

Detailed studio directions are provided upon lesson confirmation.

Teaching Philosophy

Music is more than notes.

Technique Creativity Expression Confidence

Happy Learning. Meaningful Progress.

I believe students learn best when they feel safe, curious, understood, and excited to return to the piano.

01

Joy Comes First

Music should be something students look forward to—not another source of pressure. Lessons encourage curiosity, creativity, and a genuine love of music while gradually building strong technique and musicianship.

02

Every Student Is Different

No single teaching method works for everyone. Some students learn by listening. Some learn visually. Some need to move, imagine, tell stories, or understand the “why” behind what they are playing. My job is not simply to teach the lesson. It is to discover how each student learns best.

Explore three more principles
03

Communication Is Essential

I want my students to know that their ideas matter. They are always encouraged to tell me: “I don’t understand.” “Can we try this another way?” “I really love this piece.” “This is difficult for me.” These conversations are not interruptions to learning—they are part of learning. A strong teacher-student relationship is built on trust, respect, and communication.

04

Little Missions, Big Progress

Joyful learning does not mean learning without goals. Students may receive small weekly Music Missions—a technique challenge, a listening activity, a practice goal, a creative exercise, or a musical discovery to bring back to the next lesson. The goal is not perfection. The goal is to build curiosity, independence, consistency, and the confidence to keep moving forward.

05

More Than Piano

Ultimately, I hope students leave the studio with more than the ability to play an instrument. I hope they learn how to listen, express themselves, overcome challenges, stay curious, and find confidence in their own voice.

Good music begins with good communication.

FAQ

Good questions
make good music.

How does tuition payment work?

Tuition is accepted via Zelle or cash and is due at the beginning of each month. Monthly tuition reserves the student’s regular weekly lesson time.

What is the cancellation policy?

Please provide at least 24 hours’ notice if you need to cancel or reschedule a lesson. When sufficient notice is provided, a make-up lesson may be arranged based on studio availability.

Do you offer make-up lessons?

Yes. Make-up lessons are available for eligible cancellations with at least 24 hours’ notice and are scheduled according to teacher and studio availability.

Are recitals offered?

Yes! Studio recitals are offered twice each year, giving students the opportunity to share their progress, build confidence, and celebrate music with family and fellow students. Participation is encouraged but not required.

Do you prepare students for competitions?

Absolutely. Students interested in competitions, auditions, examinations, or other performance opportunities are always welcome to discuss their goals with the teacher. Preparation plans can be developed according to the student’s level, timeline, and individual goals.

Do you offer RCM or ABRSM preparation?

Yes. Lessons can include preparation for RCM and ABRSM examinations, including repertoire, technique, musicianship, and music theory.

Are master lessons available?

For selected students seeking advanced musical development, opportunities for master lessons with university music professors and professional musicians may be available when appropriate. Please contact the studio to discuss whether this would be a good fit for the student’s current level and goals.

What happens when the teacher is on vacation?

Planned studio vacations will generally be communicated at least one month in advance so families have plenty of time to plan accordingly.

What if I have a question about lessons or my child’s progress?

Please reach out anytime. Communication between students, families, and the teacher is an important part of the learning process. Questions about practice, repertoire, progress, motivation, scheduling, or lesson goals are always welcome.
